I re-classified all 94 rows: every D (31), every A (27), every B (36), plus extra checks. There are no C, E or F rows in this batch. The notice ids (12.45M to 17.3M) are all 2011–2013 XML era. I read 7 notices for context: 12497785, 12543416, 12552163, 12513246, 16859068, 17022086, 12576023, 17281688.

No D names a winner. These Ds were confirmed against their notice:
- 1537305 (12552163): RES-3 CONTRACT_TITLE is 'Agence Paul Signac et agence Beaumonts.', so the agences are the buyer's (OPHM de Montreuil) sites.
- 2378132 (17022086): the full ORG-6 name ends 'a été déclaré infructueux' and RES-5 has no award date. The '3 titulaires seront désignés' wording is from the lot description.
- 1633917 (12576023): a design contest declared sans suite. Toth-Fasquelle is the failed would-be awardee, and RES-1 has nothing but this org.

Of the other Ds, 1974244 names a rejected bidder and 1610364 names the buyer. Only 1341883 is wrong (awarded, not void; see disagreements). Before any D goes VoidLot, it is worth checking whether its RES has CONTRACT_AWARD_DATE or CONTRACT_NUMBER set; that test is what caught 1341883.

All A winners are real companies or bodies. Points to watch when extracting:
- 1668604: the text fuses 'Sarltacavl', so the classifier's mapping to SARL TACAVL is a lookup, not literal extraction.
- 1435456: 'Grunenthal/CSP' is a lab/distributor pair kept as one string.
- 2734624 and 2734625: groupement strings with a 'GRPT' prefix.
- 1484119: 'CSL Berhing' is a typo in the source.
- 1844226, 1844229, 1844232 and 2035260: name + address + a partial-void tail. The address must be stripped, not just the tail.

B labels are acceptable, with one point for the class decision. 1813067, 1813070, 1813087, 1844213, 1844215, 1844218 and 1844224 are not multi-lot lists. They are CO-WINNERS OF ONE LOT. Notice 16859068 RES-16 reads 'Nombre de titulaires: 3', with two awarded and the rest of the lot declared sans suite. They split cleanly on '1/ … - 2/ …' or ' / ', so 'keep as is' (511 §5) under-serves them. A sub-class 'co-winners of one RES: split into N winner parties' may be worth recording.

The same notice also has co-winner rows with no void word ('1/ Gidef … - 2/ AECD … - 3/ MIC …', ORG-14 and ORG-6). Those are never in `exempted`, so this shape reaches beyond the void-word list.

Two more B checks:
- 3290486 (17281688): the full name ends 'Les lots 2 et 11 sont déclarés sans suite. Le lot 10 est déclaré infructueux', so B is confirmed.
- 2381362 and 2957546: each has a single distinct winner but covers several lots including void ones, so B is right; do not promote them to A.

Most of the D rows come from a few predicate misfires in names_an_award (crates/ingest/src/partyname.rs). Fixing these would turn the D rows into VoidLot:

This accounts for 41 of the 69 D rows. A 'Le lot N : lot X[:] <title> a été déclaré <void>' template, or treating an adjacent second designator as an alias, would catch them.
2. award_clause looks only at the word right before 'attribué', so 'n'a pas été attribué' passes (4229970). It also counts 'attribué le <date>' with no 'à <name>' (4409817/20/21).
3. The ' avec la/les société(s) ' cue misfires in a relaunch-to-negotiation sentence ('à relancer en marché négocié … avec les sociétés ayant soumissionné : lot 1 : société TIB'; 'avec les sociétés candidates').
